title: Nine Seconds Wide
subtitle: 咬与一口 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 咬与一口（生活与学习·饮食与动作）
meta: 主题语境：咬与一口（生活与学习·饮食与动作）　|　核心词汇：bite　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bite 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 my father took ① a bite of an apple that had been kept since March, and my grandmother said the taking was the whole of the decision. The ② bite, meaning the mouthful and not the apple, was nine seconds wide and was the only one he got; a bite, she said, is the only thing you can take that cannot be given back.

Every ③ bite in that house was counted, and the ④ bite on the Sunday, meaning the one taken from the middle and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever complained about. A bite, my mother said, is nine parts hunger and one part knowing whose it was; my grandmother said the hunger is the part you cannot argue with.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bite was the whole of the winter, meaning the frost and not the mouthful. The ⑥ bite, meaning the sharpness in the air and not any of that, is the only thing in a season that everybody feels and nobody can hold; a bite, he said, is either something you take from an apple or the only word that means both a mouthful and a sharpness. She said the sharpness came first.

By 1962 the ⑦ bite had become a photograph in a paper, and the paper had become an argument about the dog. The ⑧ bite of the whole thing, my father wrote in April, was nine seconds and eleven years of complaint; a bite, he said, is either the mouthful on the Sunday or the reason you learned to ask before eating. She said the asking was the part nobody remembered.

The ⑨ bite I remember is the one on the Sunday, which was taken from the middle and was never forgiven. A ⑩ bite, my grandmother said in 1965, is the only thing that improves by being shared; every bite, she said, is a sharpness that has agreed to look like a mouthful. He said the sharpness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 一口（咬下的一口）
B. n. 一口（指咬下的那一口，与苹果相对）
C. 固定搭配：take a bite of 咬一口……
D. n. 一口（指屋里每一口）
E. n. 一口（指星期天那一口）
F. n. 刺痛；凛冽（指冬天的刺骨寒气）
G. n. 凛冽（抽象：空气里那种锐利）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bite of an apple that had been kept since March
The bite, meaning the mouthful and not the apple
bite was the whole of the winter
The bite, meaning the sharpness in the air
the bite had become a photograph in a paper
The bite of the whole thing
A bite, my grandmother said in 1965

answers.why: take a bite of 意为“咬一口……”，1946 年父亲咬了一口三月起就存着的苹果。
bite 意为“一口”，指咬下的那一口而不是苹果，它宽九秒，也是他唯一得到的一口。
bite 指屋里每一口，那屋里每一口都是数着吃的。
bite 指星期天那一口（从中间咬下的那一口），是唯一有人抱怨过的。
bite 意为“刺痛、凛冽”，指冬天的刺骨寒气，叔叔说 bite 就是那个冬天的全部。
bite 为抽象用法，指空气里那种锐利，是一个季节里人人都感觉得到、却谁也抓不住的东西。
bite 意为“一口、咬”，到 1962 年这个 bite 成了报纸上的一张照片。
bite 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，父亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九秒钟和十一年的抱怨。
bite 意为“一口”，我记得的是星期天那一口，它是从中间咬下的，从没被原谅。
bite 为抽象总称，祖母说一口是唯一会因为被分享而变好的东西。
